projective_bundle_basis.module_map: For a projective bundle of relative dimension q, the reviewed1.13 basis is b_j=xi^j, 0≤j≤q. The new elements c_m=(xi−1)^m are related by c_m=sum_(j=0)^m (−1)^(m−j) binom(m,j)b_j.
projective_bundle_basis.inverse: The inverse map is b_j=sum_(m=0)^j binom(j,m)c_m, by xi=1+(xi−1). Both transformations are triangular over the base K ring with diagonal1; their composites are the polynomial identities (1+(xi−1))^j=xi^j and ((1+z)−1)^m=z^m. Thus the map from the free module with basis c_0,…,c_q to the one with basis b_0,…,b_q is an explicit module isomorphism.
projective_bundle_basis.element: In particular, c_q=(xi−1)^q is a basis element and is a product of exactly q differences of line-bundle classes; repetition of the same class is permitted by the printed existential phrase.

tower_basis.construction: Write the tower as X=X_0←X_1←…←X_m=X-prime, with X_j=P(F_(j−1)) over X_(j−1) of relative dimension q_j. Pull each tautological line class zeta_j to the top X-prime.
tower_basis.map: At each stage the actual projective-bundle formula identifies the direct sum of q_j+1 copies of K(X_(j−1)) with K(X_j), by (a_0,…,a_qj)↦sum_a f_j^*(a_a)(zeta_j−1)^a. Its inverse is the basis-coordinate map. Composing these maps yields the K(X)-basis consisting of all products over j of (zeta_j−1)^(a_j), with 0≤a_j≤q_j.
tower_basis.top_element: Choose a_j=q_j at every stage. The resulting basis element has exactly sum_j q_j=r factors. Enumerate the pulled-back zeta_j with q_j repetitions each as xi_1,…,xi_r; then it is precisely the proposed current product from1 to r.
tower_basis.dimension: Each projective stage is smooth of constant relative dimension q_j on the rank-constant pieces used by the author. Relative dimensions add under this composition, giving sum_j q_j=r, the r explicitly defined on414.

counterexamples.relative_dimension_zero: Take X=Spec k and X-prime=X, arising from rank-one flag data. Here r=0 and K(X-prime)=Z with basis1. Every line bundle on the point is k, so each line class is1. The printed product from0 to0 is xi_0−1=0 and cannot be a basis element. The corrected empty product from1 to0 is1, exactly the basis element.
counterexamples.relative_dimension_one: Take X=Spec k and X-prime=P^1_k, which is the complete flag scheme of a rank-two vector space. The corrected1.13 gives basis1,xi and380 gives (1−xi^(-1))^2=0. With delta=xi−1=xi(1−xi^(-1)), this is delta^2=0; the basis map identifies K(P^1) with Z[delta]/(delta^2). Every line bundle is O(a): on the two affine-line charts, invertible modules are free because k[t] is a PID; their transition on the overlap is a unit c t^a of k[t,t^(-1)], and rescaling a trivialization removes c. Hence its class is xi^a, for some integer a. The formula (1+delta)^a=1+a delta holds also for negative a because (1+delta)^(-1)=1−delta. Therefore every printed two-factor product (xi^a−1)(xi^b−1)=ab delta^2=0, and no choice of those two line classes can make it a Z-basis element.
